name: Paranormal Shakti on-site: hippocampal signal, 8-coil cross
summary: The on-site hippocampus session of Murphy's retired Paranormal Shakti (about 2012-2015), which the vendor offered to investigators for 'intuitive perceptions' at a site: 30 min of the hippocampal signal alternating between the two stereo channels of a 4-coil cross on each temporal lobe.
setting: On site during an investigation, at a time of geomagnetic quiet (vendor).
schedule: Vendor: after 6 temporal sessions, do 3 frontal ones (murphy-paranormal-shakti-frontal), but not in the 3 days before an investigation, because it says the frontal session lowers sensitivity. The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days.
notes: Coils form a cross on each temporal lobe: FT7 (front), C5 (top), TP7 (back) and T9 (bottom) on the left, FT8, C6, TP8 and T10 on the right; the sites are an inference from the vendor's description. Following 'begin with the left channel vertical and the right channel horizontal', track 1 (the left stereo channel) drives the top and bottom coils (C5, T9, C6, T10) and track 2 (the right channel) the front and back coils (FT7, TP7, FT8, TP8). The signal alternates between the two groups slowly, one whole signal per switch with about 4 s of silence in between; the Paranormal Shakti pages give no alternation speed, and the 8 Coil Shakti's 'fast' mode (a switch every half-second), which its pages say 'emerged as the most effective' in the original developers' lab tests, is not used. Polarity follows the 8 Coil Shakti coil chart (the Paranormal Shakti pages do not repeat it): each pair is one + and one - coil, so C5 (top) and FT7 (front) on the left and T10 (bottom) and TP8 (back) on the right get the reversed signal (weight -1), while T9, TP7, C6 and FT8 get it as is. The hippocampal ('LTP') file is proprietary; it is approximated by the point table of the project's other 8 Coil Shakti hippocampal sessions: four theta bursts, each of 4 biphasic pulses 9 ms apart (about 110 Hz, the nearest the Shakti's 3-ms points allow to the 100 Hz of Larson & Lynch's theta bursts), one burst every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal), 0.74 s per train. The vendor also describes the cross 'raised up' above the temporo-parietal region. The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users of an earlier version of its signals, mostly with hippocampal signals, and advises lowering the intensity by one-third if it happens. Experiences during or after such a session are not evidence about the site. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The product is retired; this file is of historical interest. Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once on fear or distress.
